title: Rav Yehoshua
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Pesachim 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.53b): “Rav Yehoshua said: Rava expounded.” Perhaps he was the father of the well-known Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. Dikdukei Soferim records an omission at “Rav Yehoshua.” In [Shabbat 151b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.151b.5) we find: “Rabbi Levi said: Rav Pappi said: Rabbi Yehoshua said: After three days his belly splits open,” etc. There the reading should be Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin, as explained in his entry.[^1]

notes.text: The proposed father-son identification and correction to Yehoshua of Sikhnin are Hyman’s. Hyman writes ליתא תיבת רב יהושע, which may concern the complete designation or just Rav before Yehoshua; “an omission at” leaves its extent open. דק״ס stands for Dikdukei Soferim. The William Davidson Hebrew text of [Shabbat 151b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.151b.5) reads Rabbi Levi, Rav Pappi and Rabbi Yehoshua; that title does not itself identify Yehoshua with the subject of this entry.
